questions.question: What main point is given in the opening example of the garden?
questions.answer: Different readers will benefit at different levels, and even if someone cannot grasp everything, he can still receive a meaningful share.

questions.question: According to the passage, how many reasons make this work hard to understand?
questions.answer: Five reasons are given.

questions.question: What is the first reason for the difficulty of the book?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own personal understanding and observations, mainly for himself, not shaped around how others usually think.

questions.question: How does the second reason connect the subject of the book to its difficulty?
questions.answer: The book discusses the oneness of Allah in a very wide and deep way, so many readers cannot take in all of it at once.

questions.question: Why can one sentence become very long in this treatise?
questions.answer: A single sentence may carry a large truth that should not be broken apart, and that truth may need many introductory points first.

questions.question: Why does the fourth reason say some discussions become lengthy?
questions.answer: Many topics include numerous proofs and pieces of evidence, so the explanation grows long through repeated demonstration.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of readers may struggle with that long method of proof?
questions.answer: People with limited understanding may find it hard to follow.

questions.question: What special spiritual time is mentioned in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The lights or inspirations of the treatise are said to have come during Ramadan.

questions.question: What personal conditions affected the writing process in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The writer was distressed, physically ill, and wrote quickly without going back to revise the first draft.

questions.question: Why did the writer feel he should not reorganize or correct the work?
questions.answer: He felt the writing was not coming purely from his own choice, so changing it according to his own thoughts seemed unfitting.

questions.question: Besides haste and illness, what other feature added to the difficulty of understanding the book?
questions.answer: Some Arabic sections were included, and one whole part in Arabic was separated into its own work.

questions.question: What happened to the First Station mentioned at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It was entirely in Arabic and was removed to stand as a separate work.

questions.question: What overall attitude does the passage teach readers to have before beginning this treatise?
questions.answer: Readers should be humble, patient, and ready to benefit as much as they can, even if they do not understand every part.

questions.question: What reassurance is given to readers who may not understand the whole treatise?
questions.answer: They are told that no one will leave without gaining something from it.

questions.question: In the image of the garden, what do the unreachable fruits represent?
questions.answer: They represent parts of the treatise that some readers may not be able to fully understand.

questions.question: In that same image, what does the fruit within reach represent?
questions.answer: It represents the amount of understanding and benefit a person is able to gain.

questions.question: What does the garden image suggest about differences among readers?
questions.answer: It suggests that readers do not all have the same ability, but the work still has benefit for each of them.

questions.question: Why is the first cause important for understanding the tone of the book?
questions.answer: It shows the book comes from a personal mode of reflection rather than from a style adjusted for a broad audience.

questions.question: What makes the second cause different from the first cause?
questions.answer: The first concerns the writer’s personal method, while the second concerns the greatness and depth of the subject itself.

questions.question: What subject is described as being presented in a highly comprehensive way?
questions.answer: The affirmation of Allah’s unity is presented in a very complete and far-reaching way.

questions.question: Why would breaking up a long sentence be a problem in the third cause?
questions.answer: It could damage the wholeness of the truth being explained.

questions.question: What is meant by saying one proof needs many preliminaries?
questions.answer: It means a conclusion may depend on several earlier explanations before it can be understood properly.

questions.question: How does the fourth cause add another kind of difficulty beyond sentence length?
questions.answer: It shows that not only the wording but also the large number of proofs can make the discussion heavy for some readers.

questions.question: Which cause includes both spiritual inspiration and human weakness together?
questions.answer: The fifth cause includes both, since it mentions inspiration in Ramadan along with distress, illness, and haste.

questions.question: How did the writing conditions in the fifth cause affect the final form of the work?
questions.answer: The work remained in an unrevised form and therefore became harder to understand.

questions.question: What can a careful student learn from all five causes taken together?
questions.answer: The difficulty of the book comes from both the greatness of its message and the difficult conditions under which it was written.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the opening warning in this passage?
questions.answer: It prepares readers not to expect easy understanding of everything while still encouraging them to benefit.

questions.question: How does the comparison to a garden help explain fairness in benefiting from the work?
questions.answer: It shows the work is not limited to one level of reader, since each person takes what he can while others may reach more.

questions.question: What number of causes is announced before they are listed?
questions.answer: Five causes are announced.

questions.question: What is the basic idea of the first cause in simple words?
questions.answer: The book follows the writer’s own inner path of understanding instead of a commonly adjusted teaching style.

questions.question: What feature of the book’s subject leads to the second cause?
questions.answer: Its subject is the oneness of Allah explained in a vast and elevated way.

questions.question: What explanation is given for very long sentences in the third cause?
questions.answer: Long sentences are used so a large truth can stay connected and complete.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why are introductory points needed before a proof?
questions.answer: They prepare the mind so the proof can be understood in its full meaning.

questions.question: What does the fourth cause reveal about the book’s method of argument?
questions.answer: It often supports its points with many separate evidences instead of only one or two.

questions.question: How could many proofs help and also challenge a reader?
questions.answer: They can strengthen certainty, but they can also make the discussion long and demanding.

questions.question: What emotional and physical state is described in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The writer describes being troubled inwardly and suffering from illness while writing.

questions.question: What decision about revision is described in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The first draft was left without later editing or rearranging.

questions.question: What language issue is mentioned as an extra source of difficulty?
questions.answer: Some parts remained in Arabic, including a major section that was later separated.

questions.question: If a student feels overwhelmed by this treatise, which idea from the passage should encourage him most?
questions.answer: He should remember that partial benefit still matters and that full understanding of every part is not required to gain something valuable.

questions.question: What balanced message is given in the first paragraph about understanding and benefit?
questions.answer: Complete understanding is not promised to everyone, but some benefit is promised to everyone.

questions.question: Why is the image of people with longer arms included in the garden example?
questions.answer: It shows that some readers have greater capacity than others, and the work serves all of them, not just one kind.

questions.question: What does the passage do immediately after the garden example?
questions.answer: It introduces five specific reasons why the work is difficult.

questions.question: In the first reason, whose understanding guided the writing?
questions.answer: The writer’s own understanding guided it.

questions.question: How is this writing method contrasted with many other books?
questions.answer: Other books are often written to fit the understanding of readers, but this one was not shaped that way.

questions.question: What religious truth is named in the second reason as especially wide and deep?
questions.answer: The truth of Allah’s unity is the central matter described that way.

questions.question: What is the effect of presenting that truth in such a complete form?
questions.answer: It makes the topics very expansive, deep, and at times lengthy.

questions.question: In the third reason, why is keeping a truth unbroken so important?
questions.answer: Because separating it too much could weaken how clearly and fully it is conveyed.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage show between proofs and preparation?
questions.answer: Proofs often depend on a good deal of groundwork being laid first.

questions.question: In the fourth reason, about how many proofs may be used for demonstration?
questions.answer: Sometimes as many as ten or twenty proofs may be included.

questions.question: What effect can that many proofs have on the discussion?
questions.answer: It can make the discussion feel extended and difficult for some readers.

questions.question: What month is connected with the spiritual origin of the treatise’s insights?
questions.answer: Ramadan is connected with those insights.

questions.question: What practical circumstances made the writing process more difficult in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The writer was in distress, had several illnesses, wrote quickly, and did not revise afterward.

questions.question: What belief about the source of the writing kept the writer from editing it freely?
questions.answer: He felt the writing was not simply a product of his own personal will, so changing it based on his own ideas seemed improper.

questions.question: What final detail in the passage shows that language itself could be a barrier for some readers?
questions.answer: Part of the material was in Arabic, and a fully Arabic section was set apart as its own work.

questions.question: What expectation should a reader avoid when beginning this treatise?
questions.answer: A reader should not expect to understand every matter fully from the start.

questions.question: What hopeful point is still made for every reader?
questions.answer: Every reader can still receive some share of benefit.

questions.question: What lesson about human ability comes from the example of reaching fruit in a garden?
questions.answer: People have different limits and capacities, so they do not all receive the same amount.

questions.question: What is the first listed cause of difficulty in the book?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own perspective and personal understanding rather than being adjusted to others.

questions.question: How does the second cause describe the treatment of Divine unity?
questions.answer: It describes it as presented in a very comprehensive way connected to a supreme divine manifestation.

questions.question: Why would such treatment be hard for many readers?
questions.answer: Because the themes become very wide, deep, and sometimes long.

questions.question: What writing choice explained in the third cause can make reading slower?
questions.answer: A single sentence may carry so much meaning that it stretches over a long space.

questions.question: According to the third cause, what must often come before one proof?
questions.answer: Many preparatory explanations must come first.

questions.question: What is the central problem described in the fourth cause?
questions.answer: The large number of evidences used for one matter can make the explanation lengthy and difficult.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the writer’s condition while composing the treatise?
questions.answer: He was troubled, physically unwell, and writing in haste.

questions.question: How did those conditions affect editing?
questions.answer: The first draft was not revised.

questions.question: What inward reason is given for not correcting the text afterward?
questions.answer: The writer felt it would be inappropriate to reshape the material according to his own later thoughts.

questions.question: Name two additional features from the fifth cause that could make the work harder for some readers.
questions.answer: Some passages were in Arabic, and the first major section was entirely in Arabic and then separated from this work.

questions.question: What two ideas are held together in the opening lines of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage joins warning with encouragement by saying the work is hard, yet still beneficial.

questions.question: How does the garden example help a student approach a challenging religious text?
questions.answer: It teaches the student to take the amount he can reach and not become discouraged by what is beyond him.

questions.question: After the opening image, what structure does the passage use to explain the difficulty?
questions.answer: It lists five distinct causes one by one.

questions.question: What does the first cause tell us about the origin of the book’s explanations?
questions.answer: They came from the writer’s own reflections and were written in his own way.

questions.question: Why might a work written mainly from personal understanding be harder for others?
questions.answer: Because it may not follow the patterns or explanations most readers expect.

questions.question: What makes the second cause mainly about content rather than style?
questions.answer: It focuses on the greatness and depth of the topic being discussed, especially Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What effect does that kind of content have on the length and depth of the book?
questions.answer: It makes the subjects very broad, very deep, and at times extended.

questions.question: In the third cause, what is protected by letting one sentence run very long?
questions.answer: The full integrity of a major truth is protected from being broken apart.

questions.question: What does the third cause teach about careful reasoning?
questions.answer: It shows that deep conclusions often need groundwork before they can be properly proven.

questions.question: What does the fourth cause suggest about the book’s approach to certainty?
questions.answer: It seeks to support claims strongly by piling up many evidences.

questions.question: Why can that strong approach still become a challenge for readers?
questions.answer: Because too many demonstrations can become hard to track, especially for weaker readers.

questions.question: What spiritual source is mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The treatise’s insights are linked to the blessed light of Ramadan.

questions.question: What human limitations are mentioned alongside that spiritual source?
questions.answer: Distress, sickness, haste, and the absence of revision are all mentioned.

questions.question: How did the writer’s view of his role in the writing affect the final text?
questions.answer: Since he did not see himself as acting purely by personal choice, he avoided reshaping the work afterward.

questions.question: What final conclusion can be drawn from the whole passage about why the treatise is difficult?
questions.answer: Its difficulty comes from a combination of profound subject matter, detailed proof, personal writing style, and challenging circumstances of composition.
